Simon's near-decomposability ([THEORY-661](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-661.md)) is about interaction strengths: interactions within subsystems much stronger than between them. A correlation length measures statistical dependence. In a system with short-range interactions, a block of side L in d dimensions has interactions across its boundary in number of order L^(d−1) against L^d inside, so large blocks meet Simon's condition whatever the correlation length, at a critical point as elsewhere. So a finite correlation length is not what gives near-decomposability, and an unbounded one does not take it away.
